section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1967
title: 12 The maximum incidence of suicides was observed in the State of West Bengal (6513) followed by Tamil Nadu (5369) and Uttar Pradesh (5137) accounting for 16·8%, 13·8% and 13·2% of total suicides reported in the country respectively. As in the previous year also, the incidence in Jammu and Kashmir is negligible viz. only 7 cases during 1967 as against 31 during 1966. With a view to studying the pattern of suicidal deaths with respect to population, the volume of suicidal deaths for one hundred thousand of population was studied and incidentally the maximum volume of suicides was again observed in West Bengal (15·7) followed by Tamil Nadu (14·3) but in U.P. where the incidence was as high as in Tamil Nadu, volume of suicides was only 6·1. Incidence in all the Union Territories was only 3·1% of all-India total but the volume varies widely. Pondicherry recorded as high as 42·5 while in Manipur only 6 cases were reported (volume 0·6). Among the important cities Bangalore (13·6) recorded the maximum volume followed closely by Delhi (13·4). The relevant statistics are furnished in Table 10. TABLE—10
